To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RNA binding protein, HuR is a novel component of the chromatoid body and is required for the storage and translation of specific ARE-mRNAs during spermatogenesis.

HuR, an RNA binding protein known in somatic tissues to regulate the stability/translation AU-rich containing mRNAS (ARE-mRNAS), localizes to a specific cytoplasmic structure in the germ cells of the mouse testis, the chromatoid body, where it associates with its target mRNAS.
the RNA binding protein, HuR, is localized in the CB of round spermatids and then traffics to polysomes as the cells differentiate, together with its target ARE-containing mRNas, Brd2, and GCNF.

the regulation of mRNA stability and translation in the context of male germ cell development.
the mechanisms by which mRNA is regulated and stored in germ cells.
the mechanisms that regulate the translation of specific messenger RNAs during the development of male germ cells.

HuR is a key player in the regulation of mRNA storage and the temporal regulation of translation in male germ cells.
